records.title: Uniform additive and multiplicative indicator concentration
records.statement: For every nonconstant centered indicator over a prime field, simultaneous additive and multiplicative basis concentration obeys the proved size/origin caps, including constant character and point-mass cases. For S subset F_p^*, approximate supports of sizes r,s with projection norm errors epsilon,eta satisfy rs >= (1-epsilon^2)(1-eta^2)(p-1)(p-|S|)^2/(p|S|^2). This completes A-TRANSFER.
records.remaining: No Paley clique asymptotic, metric or original word-model classification follows. Origin point masses are explicit degeneracies. No novelty or external-review claim.

records.title: Fixed-prime good degrees are automatic
records.statement: For each fixed prime p, rationally split integral polynomials with all coefficients nonzero modulo p have an effectively p-automatic set of degrees. Weighted-cycle analysis decides whether the nonzero base-p digit counts of degree+1 are bounded, and their maximum if bounded.
records.remaining: No uniform all-prime cycle exclusion or c(p)=p-1 proof. Prior partial mark is retained.

records.title: Unrestricted two-coordinate exclusion for a bounded third coordinate
records.statement: Exact signed-divisor and discriminant certificates exclude every integer solution of the source symmetric cubic with any coordinate of absolute value at most 5000; the other coordinates are unrestricted. Symmetry transfers the complete fiber exclusion.
records.remaining: No bound on all coordinates or full integer nonexistence theorem. Prior partial mark preserved.

records.title: Constructive smooth values for every linear polynomial
records.statement: For every f(n)=an+b with a nonzero integer and every epsilon>0, an explicit positive integer exponential subsequence has f(n) nonzero and supported on one fixed finite set of primes. Consequently infinitely many values are n^epsilon-smooth, including a<0 and b=0.
records.remaining: Higher-degree polynomials remain unresolved. No originality claim.

records.title: Complete integer nonextension of a specified square-sum seed
records.statement: The specified four-by-four square-sum seed has no new integer neighbor on either side, with the new integer unrestricted. Opposite integer translations preserve this fact.
records.remaining: This does not exclude all five-by-five square-sum sets or rational neighbors. Squared scaling preserves equations but need not preserve integer nonextension.

records.title: Exact two-sided integral rescaling criterion
records.statement: A positive rational two-sided product tuple admits a rational scale making both sides integral exactly when all cross-products are integral; the valuation intervals give a simultaneous scale. Source tuple splits were checked against this condition.
records.remaining: Positivity/distinctness and the full requested tuple construction remain separate. This is a reduction, not a catalog existence proof.

records.title: Exact one-colour finite-field remainder dimension
records.statement: For every positive n, the minimum largest affine-subspace dimension of R under the source admissibility condition with k=1 is n-1. A nonempty complement is midpoint-closed and affine; a hyperplane complement attains the bound.
records.remaining: The general sharp function for k>=2 remains unresolved.

records.title: Conjugation-fixed partition parity product
records.statement: Conjugation pairs nonfixed partitions. The integer-input partition count modulo two equals the coefficient of the locally finite product over positive integer parts and unordered positive nonintegral conjugate pairs, with pair weight its trace.
records.remaining: Distinct-value divisibility and the all-field parity targets are unresolved. Unit orbits alone repeat one partition count.

records.title: Exact finite subset-sum state algorithm
records.statement: For a finite abelian group and g nonzero, sequences avoiding g have an exact subset-sum DAG: every permitted appended term strictly increases the reachable-sum set. Longest paths determine the relative Davenport constant.
records.remaining: The universal monotonicity target is not proved. This is a finite exact method.

records.title: Certified lower bound for the sum-difference entropy constant
records.statement: The rational law on {1,3,5} with probabilities (913,79,8)/1000 has (H(X-Xprime)-H(X))/(H(X+Xprime)-H(X)) strictly between 1.39778460678578706484097027537185551 and 1.39778460678578706484097027537185552. Exact rational logarithm bounds certify that the least universal constant exceeds 139/100.
records.remaining: The exact universal constant, its equality to two, and global optimization are unresolved. This certifies an existing counted construction; no sixth attempt or novelty claim.

records.title: Exact rainbow optimum with one monochromatic parity class
records.statement: When all even integers have the same color, the maximum asymptotic normalized rainbow-Schur count is 9/22, with uniform discretization control for the odd coloring.
records.remaining: No reduction of unrestricted colorings to this subclass. Prior return bound and mark retained.

records.title: Exact optimum in the two-prefix palette family
records.statement: The specified two-prefix three-color template has exact asymptotic optimum 3/7; the checked uniform parity refinements give at most 60/121.
records.remaining: These are restricted templates, below the preserved return bound 50368/90905. No proof of convergence for all unrestricted maxima.

records.title: Fractional obstruction to the first cube relaxation
records.statement: The retained all-size fractional cube-hyperedge construction has density 17/24, showing that the specified linear relaxation cannot prove the desired sharp density.
records.remaining: A fractional model obstruction, not an actual cube-free set counterexample.

records.title: Counterexample to a diagonal-progression sufficient lemma
records.statement: The explicit retained set defeats the proposed auxiliary diagonal-progressions criterion while containing a genuine mixed cube.
records.remaining: It refutes the auxiliary proof lemma, not Q1960 or a cube-free density bound.

records.title: Five-eighths bound in the high-odd-density branch
records.statement: The high-odd-density branch of the cube-free analysis proves the five-eighths density bound under its stated branch assumptions.
records.remaining: The intermediate-density regime and the universal bound remain unresolved.

records.title: Finite-summand exclusion near the squares
records.statement: With the source o(sqrt(X)) cumulative square-perturbation error, a sumset decomposition cannot have a finite summand of size at least two; two fixed shifts give the counting bound and a necessary error scale Omega(X^(1/4)).
records.remaining: Sparse infinite/infinite decompositions are not excluded. Original partial mark is retained.

records.title: Genus-five four-row cover and a two-row Pell boundary
records.statement: Four distinct fixed square-sum rows produce the specified degree-sixteen genus-five cover. Two fixed rows allow unbounded Pell-based extensions with both signs permitted.
records.remaining: Uniformity on the four-row cover is conditional; the unrestricted bipartite minimum problem is not reduced to a clique theorem.

records.title: Reciprocal factors in shifted cyclotomic families
records.statement: Reciprocal irreducible factors in the source product-plus-one family and unequal-degree sum family are cyclotomic. Exact finite factor controls retain their degree conditions.
records.remaining: Irreducibility of the remaining noncyclotomic factor is not established. The original two partial marks and scopes remain unchanged.

records.title: Two-factor signed-distinct Lehmer exclusion
records.statement: The signed distinct two-factor case reduces to the retained exact factor identity, which forces equality of the two parameters and violates distinctness.
records.remaining: Larger factor counts and the full Lehmer-style equation remain unresolved.

records.title: Two-variable regularity threshold
records.statement: The minimal threshold is r(1)=1 vacuously and r(2)=2. A nonregular two-variable equation with opposite signs has unequal coefficient ratio; a nonzero prime valuation of that ratio gives a two-coloring by valuation bands with no monochromatic solution.
records.remaining: No threshold proof for every number of variables. Same-sign coefficients have no positive solution.

records.title: RCA0 three-color single-difference avoidance
records.statement: For every coded countable abelian group and nonzero b, the translation graph of x-y=b has degree at most two. Greedy coloring in the enumeration gives a three-color avoidance proof in RCA0.
records.remaining: This is a single-equation subcase. It does not classify the ring/matrix assertion or imply a two-color reversal. Prior partial mark retained.

records.title: Known infinite elasticity in quadratic orders
records.statement: The sourced split-prime-dividing-conductor criterion realizes infinite elasticity in the retained real-quadratic setup, using all powers of a suitable split prime.
records.remaining: This is a prior literature subcase; the finite prescribed elasticities in all fields remain unresolved.

records.title: Exact least-common-multiple identity for divisor moments
records.statement: The kth shifted-prime divisor moment equals the exact sum over ordered prime tuples of floor(X/lcm(p1-1,...,pk-1)). Coincidences and gcd factors are retained.
records.remaining: No asymptotic constant or uniform error after summing the floor terms is proved.

records.title: Atomic power monoid for all odd-prime reciprocal generators
records.statement: In M generated by 1/p for every odd prime, a zero-integer-part element has only finitely many divisors by the canonical residue form. Subtracting the minimum integer part proves every finite set has an MCD. M is atomic, so the sourced atomic-MCD theorem makes its finitary power monoid atomic.
records.remaining: This rules out one accumulating rank-one candidate, not all almost-atomic Puiseux monoids. Prior necessary-condition partial is preserved.

records.title: Complete product-one threshold verification for S3
records.statement: All possible ordering products of multiplicity vectors prove d(S3)=3 and E(S3)=9: all 126 length-four and 2002 length-nine multisets pass the respective tests, with exact length-three and length-eight lower witnesses.
records.remaining: One finite group, already in known dihedral results; arbitrary groups remain open. The earlier universal lower-bound partial remains unchanged.

records.title: Known realization of every two-element length set
records.statement: The reviewed primary Theorem 1.1 realizes every {a,b}, 2<=a<b, by the length-family expression {2,b-a+2}+(a-2){1}. The new complete finite power-set enumeration covers all 4096 normalized sets through maximum twelve.
records.remaining: The two-element theorem is sourced prior work. General finite length sets and a uniform witness-size bound remain open; the old partial/archive issue is retained.

records.title: Known half-factorial class groups for countable groups
records.statement: The reviewed Geroldinger-Gobel theorem supplies half-factorial monoid-generating subsets for Warfield groups, including all countable groups, and the cited prime-class realization theorem yields corresponding Dedekind domains.
records.remaining: This is known literature. Arbitrary abelian groups require compatible prime-class selection; unions, quotients and compact limits can lose the needed properties.

records.title: Graded BF exclusion and a well-founded non-BF monoid
records.statement: Connected N-graded domains are BF by additive degree; the filtered case with a domain leading ring has the same degree argument. An explicit infinite-rank cancellative monoid has ACCP and all lengths n>=2 for x, using a canonical integer budget and disjoint atom families.
records.remaining: The graded result is known background. The illustrative monoid is not finitely generated; no ring ACCP or finite-presentation counterexample is claimed.

records.title: Every B2 target reaches its own stopping condition
records.statement: All 81 catalog questions have five reviewed substantive failed full-target routes (405 total); A-TRANSFER is solved locally. Partial proofs do not reset counters. The same retained agent completed ten catalog packets and the broader proof; root completed the other 71 catalog questions and the final filing.
records.remaining: The catalog questions remain unresolved. Source, shell and service failures are excluded; new finite checks do not recover the original missing archive.

review_policy: Per-result internal proof and scope review; no novelty or external peer-review claim
